## Purpose

What each category of test is there to prove, and which claims rest on it. The suite is run in
full and again with every gated code disabled (`TKIT_TIER_A_ONLY=1`); at the last publish,
98 tests passed in the first mode and 98 in the
second, at commit `ac911c3`. Tests that need an optional code (TORAX, FreeGSNKE,
ASCOT5, Aurora) or a downloaded file skip cleanly when it is absent.

The code now has a private hosted repository and the continuous-integration workflow runs on
every change ([OQ-3](/Blog/toktoit/decisions.qmd#oq-3)). Until it has passed, these counts come from runs made before each publish,
not from CI.

## Categories

| category | proves | examples | claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| **unit** | each component does what its interface says, in isolation | config parsing and scalar coercion; domain membership under `jit`/`vmap`; guard decisions; ensemble shapes; IMAS round trips; provenance validation; run tracking (local record, alerts, failed status, the Simvue mirror offline); smoke tests of ASCOT5 and Aurora | [C-024](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-024), [C-031](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-031) |
| **conservation** | the discrete equations conserve what the physics conserves | single-step particle and energy balance; every step's balance reconstructed from a full run's trace; stored-energy identity over a run; TORAX's per-step energy and particle balance on the ITER benchmark, with the edge flux computed independently | [C-026](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-026), [C-027](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-027), [C-035](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-035), [C-036](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-036), [C-037](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-037), [C-039](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-039) |
| **physics** | responses have the right sign and shape | more heating gives higher temperature; critical-gradient stiffness; Gaussian RF power, position and response; MAST-U equilibrium current, axis, completeness and resampling | [C-017](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-017), [C-018](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-018), [C-020](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-020), [C-021](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-021) |
| **regression** | known results stay known | 100 compiled toy steps; Newton converges quadratically and where Picard stalls; loop equals TORAX's own driver; tracked command-line run end to end; reference reproduced; first-order time convergence; guard identities; TORAX conversion identities | [C-001](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-001), [C-003](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-003), [C-005](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-005), [C-006](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-006), [C-007](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-007), [C-009](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-009), [C-010](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-010), [C-014](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-014), [C-015](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-015), [C-040](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-040) |
| **diff** | derivatives exist and are right | gradients through 20 toy steps and three TORAX steps against finite differences; forward mode equals reverse mode | [C-008](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-008), [C-028](/Blog/toktoit/claims.qmd#c-028) |
| **tier_a** | open code stands alone | every module labelled; every module imports with all gated packages blocked | – |

## How a claim becomes `tested`

A claim is marked `tested` only if a named test asserts it, at a tolerance no looser than the
one quoted. The test's name is in the claim's evidence column. Measured numbers that no test
pins (timings, study results) are `measured`, and say which run produced them.

## Honest limits

- Most tests were written by the same agent that wrote the code they test. The identity tests
  (wrapped equals unwrapped, loop equals TORAX's own driver, recomputed equals reported) are the
  strongest, because they compare against something the agent did not write.
- The IMAS round trip is self-consistent by construction and missed [K-007](/Blog/toktoit/ceilings.qmd#k-007); see
  [IMAS adapters](imas-adapters.qmd#post-mortem-export); it is now fixed and covered by
  tests that compare against the source codes' own values.
- No physicist has reviewed the physics tests yet (M1 gate).
